To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatio‐temporality of mining‐induced microseismicity is characterized by a diffusion exponent H= 0.18, and by an increase of H when considering only a sub‐set of the most energetic micro‐earthquaks as mainshocks.
the stress diffusion exponent is found by analyzing the spatial distribution of the aftershocks of a seismic system, and that the diffusion exponent increases for more energetic events.
the spatial distribution of aftershocks of mining-induced seismicity changes with time, and that this change is consistent with a subdiffusion mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spatial distribution of mining‐induced micro‐earthquake activity, in the vicinity of the main events, and the analysis of the time evolution of this spatial distribution.
the analysis of the spatio‐temporally correlated events occuring in a seismic system.
the spatio‐temporality of the seismicity induced by mining activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the seismicity in this mining‐induced system is the result of a stress diffusion mechanism on a fractal fault network, and that the seismic activity can be considered as a self‐organizing criticality process.

the spatio‐temporally correlated seismicity of a mining‐industrially induced seismicity is characterized by the presence of a diffusion mechanism of the stress, with the exponent H = 0.18 ± 0.03, which is consistent with the results found in other mining and natural systems.
stress diffusion is a mechanism that is likely to occur in mining‐induced systems, but that it is only one of the mechanisms at work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatio‐temporally correlated events, i.e., those which can be considered as the after‐events of a main event, follow a stress diffusion process.

the spatio‐temporally correlated seismic activity in a mining‐seismicity system exhibits a diffusive behavior, with a diffusion exponent H ∼ 0.2, which is in good agreement with the values obtained in the laboratory.
the spatio‐temporally evolving correlation of mining‐induced micro‐earthquake events can be explained by a stress‐diffusion model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatio‐temporally correlated seismicity is the result of stress diffusion in an inhomogeneous fault network.
the spatio‐temporally correlated regime of a seismic system is not stationary in space, contrary to what is usually assumed in the literature.
, in a mining seismic system, stress diffusion may play a role in the spatio‐temporally complex seismic activity.
